_why: STAGE 1 SPIKE for #2058, which stays OPEN as the implementation issue. This task delivers a design document and no production code — a design-only spec against #2058 itself could never satisfy that issue, which asks for the lifting. PINNED DESIGN: Stage 1 produces a DESIGN DOCUMENT and no code. What is deliberately NOT pinned is the placement of PlanNode::Subquery relative to Expr::Subquery — that is the question Stage 1 exists to answer, and pinning it blind is what the orchestrator has already done wrong three times this session. FR-106 Phase 4 (#275, PR #280) introduced PlanNode::Subquery { kind, plan, correlation_columns } plus a 28-file consumer cascade across 9 plan modules, and is marked COMPLETE in docs/feature/FR-106-plan-path-completeness.md:172-189. The PRODUCER never landed: PlanBuilder does not lift an Expr::Subquery into the node, and StreamSource::Subquery (builder.rs:793) builds the inner plan only to derive its schema. Verified: of the 92 PlanNode::Subquery occurrences in src/, 90 are match arms and 2 are documentation mentions in sql/CLAUDE.md's own corrected prose — none is a construction; schema_propagation.rs:225 is representative, destructuring an existing node and rebuilding it. The only constructions are in tests/ (30 sites). Consequence: plan-level rules cannot see inside a subquery, so ColumnResolution — #1749's binder — does not resolve columns in subquery interiors, and a bad reference there is not caught at plan time. That is the last structural hole in the name-binding layer. #2060 has MERGED: sql/CLAUDE.md at e4c3511c4 now states subqueries are NOT plan-native and says why, so the worker no longer reads a file asserting the opposite of its own task. NOT a correctness bug: subqueries execute correctly via SubqueryAwareRowEvaluator per-row at runtime, and 302 subquery tests pass at 2fe36b329. This is binder and optimiser COVERAGE. The audit for #275 Part A recommended NOT doing this — the cascade exceeded that issue's 25-file STOP trigger — and a reviewer overrode it; that history is why the consumers exist without a producer.

anchors._note: logical.rs — 5 occurrences of `Subquery {`. The one that matters is the variant at :1210, preceded by its doc at :1182-1209 which SPECIFIES the contract every consumer must honour. That doc is the design input for this task — read it before anything else. The other 4 are match arms elsewhere in the file.

builder.rs:800 — the FROM-derived-table case. Builds the inner plan SOLELY for its schema. SubqueryKind has no derived-table variant, so whether this is in scope is a Stage-1 question, not an assumption.

column_resolution.rs — 3 occurrences. The binder's arm at :757 recurses with ctx.reset() and leaves correlation_columns UNTOUCHED, though logical.rs:1192-1193 requires resolving them against the outer plan's schema. A consumer that does not meet its own contract.
